   STAFF REPORT

 Meeting Date:  August 18, 2025
 To:  October 7th Memorial Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons Honorable
  Mayor Nazarian & Vice Mayor Mirisch
 From:  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager
  Stephanie Harris, Director of Community Services
 Subject:  Fundraising and Donor Recognition Program
 Attachment:  None

INTRODUCTION

The October 7th Memorial Ad Hoc Committee has been meeting to review the project
proposals and will be recommending a concept to the full City Council during the August
19, 2025, City Council Study Session. The City Council has already set aside $500,000
toward the October 7th Permanent Memorial project, but it is expected that the cost of the
memorial will exceed this amount and as a result, it is important to begin building out the
fundraising program.

It is the desire of the October 7th Memorial Ad Hoc Committee Liaisons to kick off the
fundraising campaign during the groundbreaking ceremony taking place on Sunday,
October 5, 2025.

DISCUSSION

At the May 13, 2025, October 7th Memorial Ad Hoc Committee Meeting, Liaisons reviewed
the previously approved fundraising campaigns for City projects such as the Beverly
Gardens Park restoration, Community Dog Park and the 9/11 Memorial. The liaisons
provided feedback indicating that this memorial site and fundraising campaign is unique
and unlike those we have done before.

Liaisons recommended staff look at other memorial recognition programs and specifically
those of Holocaust memorials. There were concerns about donor names and ensuring
that they are discrete and would not clutter the space nor overshadow the names of the
victims. It was important to the Liaison at this time to ensure victim names were included
in the memorial site.

Donation program exist for various Holocaust memorials around the world. Many do not
have donor walls or do not list the level of donations. Below are details from the Museum
of Tolerance in Los Angeles as well as the United States Holocaust Museum.
 Meeting Date: August 18, 2025

Although both are museums rather than stand alone memorials, the Ad Hoc can use the
information as a reference for the discussion.

Museum of Tolerance Los Angeles, CA
Major gift donors of the Museum of Tolerance are recognized in the appropriate category
on the donor walls in the main lobby of the Museum of Tolerance

Categories include:
  • Museum Builders: $1 million and above
  • Capital Benefactors: $500,000 - $1 million
  • Capital Pioneers: $250,000 - $500,000
  • Capital Fellows: $100,000 - $250,000
  • Capital Founders: $50,000 - $100,000
  • Capital Patrons: $25,000 - $50,000

United States Holocaust Memorial Museum (USHMM)
Founders Society recognizes donors who have made cumulative commitments of $1
million and above to the Museum.

Levels of Recognition
  • Founders - Gifts of $1 million or more
  • Pillars of Memory - Gifts of $2 million or more
  • Benefactors - Gifts of $5 million or more
  • Chairman’s Circle - Gifts of $10 million or more
  • Trustees' Circle - Gifts of $15 million or more
  • Ambassadors - Gifts of $20 million or more
  • Guardians of Memory -Gifts of $25 million or more
  • Cornerstone - Gifts of $50 million or more

Anne Frank Human Rights Memorial – Boise
The names of major donors are listed on the donor tablets near the Church Writing Table.
$500 pavers are engraved and displayed in perpetuity at the memorial. Friends of Anne
donors are listed on their website for an annual donation of $120.

New England Holocaust Memorial
Major donors are listed on two granite slabs on the memorial’s south entrance. Funding
levels were unable to be identified.

Other memorials and museums indicate that donors are recognized in newsletters, on
websites and through social media campaigns.

FISCAL IMPACT
At this time there are no fiscal impacts.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends Council Liaisons discuss the details around the October 7th Memorial
Donor Recognition Program. Items to consider are the various donation levels and
accompanying recognition. Liaisons are requested to provide recommendations that can
be brought before the full City Council at the September 9, 2025, meeting.

  Nancy Hunt-Coffey,
  City Manager
